diet.rationale: CALIBRATED: PREDIMED RCT confirms 30% CVD reduction, consistent with observational. Nuts, olive oil have RCT backing. Diet has higher causal fraction than exercise. Beta(3.0, 3.0) → mean 50%, 95% CI: 15-85%
diet.source: Diet: Less skeptical - PREDIMED RCT confirms substantial causal effect.

calibration_sources: Ballin et al. 2021 (RCT critical review, n=50k)
exercise.rationale: CALIBRATED: RCTs show exercise does not reduce mortality (Ballin 2021, n=50k). Finnish Twin Cohort 2024: identical twins discordant for PA show no mortality difference. Beta(1.2, 6.0) → mean 17%, 95% CI: 2-45%
exercise.source: Category-specific confounding priors calibrated against actual RCT versus observational discrepancies: exercise uses Ballin 2021 and the Finnish Twin Cohort; diet uses PREDIMED; medical uses the statin observational-versus-RCT discrepancy. Exercise: VERY skeptical - RCTs and twin studies show ~0 causal effect.

calibration_sources: Danaei et al. 2012 (statin RCT vs observational)
medical.rationale: CALIBRATED: Even RCT-based drugs show observational inflation. Statins: HR 0.54 observational vs 0.84 RCT (causal fraction ~28%). Beta(2.5, 4.0) → mean 38%, 95% CI: 8-73%
medical.source: Medical: Moderate skepticism - even RCT-based drugs show observational inflation.

other.rationale: Unknown intervention type; using conservative prior reflecting general observational bias from calibration data. Beta(1.2, 4.8) → mean 20%, 95% CI: 2-50%

sleep.rationale: No RCTs for sleep duration and mortality. High reverse causation risk: illness affects sleep patterns. CBT-I shows causal quality-of-life effects. Beta(1.5, 4.5) → mean 25%, 95% CI: 3-58%
sleep.source: Sleep: Skeptical - no RCT evidence for mortality.

social.rationale: Social relationships heavily confounded with SES, mental health, physical health. No RCT evidence possible for mortality endpoints. Beta(1.0, 5.5) → mean 15%, 95% CI: 1-42%
social.source: Social: Very skeptical - no RCT possible.

stress.rationale: Meditation/mindfulness RCTs show much smaller effects than observational. Stress levels heavily confounded with SES, health behaviors. Beta(1.2, 5.0) → mean 19%, 95% CI: 2-50%

calibration_sources: Taylor et al. 2014 (smoking cessation RCTs, ~56% causal)
Stockwell et al. 2016 (alcohol J-curve is bias)
substance.rationale: CALIBRATED: Smoking cessation has strong RCT backing (causal fraction ~56%). Alcohol J-curve is entirely confounded (MR shows no benefit). Beta(2.0, 4.0) → mean 33%, 95% CI: 6-68%
substance.source: Substance: Mixed - smoking has RCT backing, alcohol J-curve is confounded.

moderate_alcohol.source: Alcohol shows strong confounding - the "J-curve" is largely artifact. Mendelian randomization (Holmes 2014, Millwood 2019) shows linear harm. Abstainers include sick quitters (reverse causation). Light drinkers tend to be healthier, wealthier.

authored_residual_optimism.rationale: Authored qol_annual values were hand-shaded for personal severity; this strips residual optimism only. Beta(6, 2) -> mean 75%.
authored_residual_optimism.source: Residual-optimism prior for authored_shaded anchors: the authored mean already embeds a personal-severity judgment, so only residual author optimism is stripped, not the full placebo share.

cognitive.rationale: Cognitive-supplement effects in healthy adults rarely replicate outside industry trials; expectancy effects dominate. Beta(1.8, 7.2) -> mean 20%.
cognitive.source: Transport prior: fraction of a published/claimed effect expected to survive placebo stripping plus population transport.

fitness_function.rationale: CRF/strength gains from structured training are objective and RCT-backed; the shrink covers the indirect CRF-to-utility mapping, not the training response. Beta(5.0, 3.0) -> mean 63%.
fitness_function.source: Transport prior: fraction of a published/claimed effect expected to survive placebo stripping plus population transport.

general_vitality.rationale: Diffuse 'energy/vitality/longevity support' claims have the weakest evidence-to-feeling mapping. Beta(1.5, 8.5) -> mean 15%.
general_vitality.source: Transport prior: fraction of a published/claimed effect expected to survive placebo stripping plus population transport.

gi_symptom.rationale: Fiber/probiotic RCTs exist but endpoints are subjective and strain/formulation-specific effects transport poorly. Beta(2.8, 5.2) -> mean 35%.
gi_symptom.source: Transport prior: fraction of a published/claimed effect expected to survive placebo stripping plus population transport.

hair_skin.rationale: Finasteride hair outcomes are objective (photographic RCTs), but mapping appearance change to utility leans on proxy TTO weights. Beta(4.0, 4.0) -> mean 50%.
hair_skin.source: Transport prior: fraction of a published/claimed effect expected to survive placebo stripping plus population transport.

metabolic_symptom.rationale: Glycemic/metabolic symptom claims ride on objective markers but subjective wellbeing mapping is indirect. Beta(3.0, 5.0) -> mean 38%.
metabolic_symptom.source: Transport prior: fraction of a published/claimed effect expected to survive placebo stripping plus population transport.

mood_stress.rationale: Commercial adaptogen/mood trials are small, unregistered, and shrink in better designs; placebo share of subjective mood gains is large. Beta(2.0, 7.0) -> mean 22%.
mood_stress.source: Transport prior: fraction of a published/claimed effect expected to survive placebo stripping plus population transport.

pain_joint.rationale: OA/joint trials show very large placebo responses; GAIT found glucosamine no better than placebo on its primary endpoint. Beta(2.5, 6.0) -> mean 29%.
pain_joint.source: Transport prior: fraction of a published/claimed effect expected to survive placebo stripping plus population transport.

respiratory_airway.rationale: Airway interventions mix objective mechanics (AHI, resistance) with subjective sleepiness; sham-controlled CPAP trials show real but roughly halved subjective gains vs open-label. Beta(4.5, 4.5) -> mean 50%.
respiratory_airway.source: Transport prior: fraction of a published/claimed effect expected to survive placebo stripping plus population transport.

sexual_function.rationale: PDE5 pivotal RCTs show large placebo-adjusted IIEF deltas, and continued revealed use signals response; transport still shrinks toward a milder-severity user. Beta(5.5, 4.5) -> mean 55%.
sexual_function.source: Transport prior: fraction of a published/claimed effect expected to survive placebo stripping plus population transport.

calibration_sources: Winkler & Rief 2015 (placebo response in insomnia trials)
sleep_symptom.rationale: Placebo response averages ~64% of drug response for subjective insomnia outcomes (Winkler & Rief 2015); objective deltas are far smaller than felt ones. Beta(2.4, 5.6) -> mean 30%.
sleep_symptom.source: Transport priors are the fraction of a published or claimed effect expected to survive placebo stripping plus population transport. They reuse ConfoundingPrior purely for its Beta mechanics (mean, confidence interval, and sampling).

rct_objective_endpoint.source: Reporting/publication shrinkage for symptom endpoints. Same shape as the mortality table; the weak tiers are harsher because subjective endpoints are easier to p-hack and selectively report than hard endpoints.

animal_or_mechanistic.source: Animal-only or mechanistic: ~70% translation penalty plus publication bias.

meta_analysis_rcts.source: Meta-analysis of RCTs: ~20% publication bias, partly corrected via trim-and-fill.

rct_preregistered_hard_endpoint.source: Tiered publication-bias shrinkage by study quality. Empirical anchor: RCT + preregistered + hard endpoint has small residual inflation (winner's curse, ~10%). Examples: PCPT finasteride, CTT statin meta, SELECT semaglutide, ASPREE aspirin, EMPA-REG.

rct_standard.source: RCT standard: some publication/selective-reporting bias (~20%). Examples: BP RCTs, sleep-RCT onset latency, PREDIMED.

supplement_industry_rct.source: Supplement-industry RCT: ~50% publication bias (unregistered, short duration, surrogate endpoints, sponsor bias). Examples: NR, NMN, ashwagandha commercial RCTs.
